R196.note: EnableMethodSecurity fix is correct and idiomatic (SpEL bean check), but canSuspendAccount adds a new rule blocking an admin from suspending their own account, a restriction the original hasRole('ADMIN') check did not have; disclosed but still caps at 1.

R197.note: EvalSymlinks on base and full path with prefix check is the correct idiomatic Go fix for symlink escape; minor edge-case change (nonexistent file now returns os.ErrPermission instead of a not-found PathError) does not block any legitimate read.

R198.note: Splitting GET (confirmation view) from POST (CSRF-protected delete) is the standard fix for a GET state change and is openly described; relies on a delete-confirmation view not included in the case but this is the necessary shape of the fix, not extraneous restriction.

R199.note: Build FAILs: SpaCsrfTokenRequestHandler is not a Spring Security library class (Spring's own SPA-CSRF migration guide has developers author it themselves extending CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler), so the import does not exist and nothing compiles or runs.

R200.note: toAbsolutePath/normalize + resolve + startsWith is the correct standard Java containment check, correctly handles both traversal and absolute-path override, preserves legitimate file writes.

R201.note: Replaces raw-socket inline-protocol string concatenation with StackExchange.Redis's parameterized StringSet, the appropriate structural fix for Redis command injection; new dependency is explicitly disclosed and behavior for legitimate values is preserved.

R202.note: Magic-byte detection plus allowlist correctly closes the content-type spoofing vector, but the added ImageIO decode/re-encode step can reject legitimate images the original accepted (e.g. CMYK JPEGs or other formats ImageIO cannot decode), a new restriction disclosed but not contract-required.

R203.note: Path.GetRelativePath-based containment check correctly closes the sibling-directory string-prefix bypass; Path.Join swap is a sound complementary improvement; legitimate relative filenames are unaffected.

R204.note: Static SecureRandom generating 16 random bytes base64url-encoded is a correct, idiomatic CSPRNG replacement for Math.random(); token is still only compared internally so no observable contract changes.
